使用 RustStream 的 Kafka Broker ruststream-rdkafka 构建 Kafka 服务的指南。
Kafka 如何工作，ruststream-rdkafka 在 Kafka 与 RustStream 运行时之间处于什么位置，以及这样做的开销。
ruststream-rdkafka 在每条消息上的开销：与裸 rdkafka 客户端对照的吞吐量，以及它自身代码的指令数和内存分配次数。
ruststream-rdkafka 如何测量自己：三个循环、在真实 Broker 上的运行、受 Broker 限制的判定计算，以及代码计数。
ruststream-rdkafka 的基准测试数字测的是什么，以及不能从中得出哪些结论。
ruststream-rdkafka 的位置：在 RustStream 运行时与 rust-rdkafka 客户端之间，每个订阅一个消费者，共用一个生产者。
Kafka 主题是一组分区，每个分区都是按偏移量编号的有序记录日志，每个消费者组都读取它的全部内容。
librdkafka 消费者在自己的线程上预先拉取，每次轮询交出一条记录，并按计时器提交已存储的偏移量。
消费者组把每个分区交给一个成员；成员加入或离开时，分区通过再均衡转移。
Kafka 事务让写入多个分区的记录和已消费的偏移量一起变得可见，或者全都不可见。
一个订阅通过一个消费者读取它的全部分区；workers(n, by_key) 把记录分到按分区划分的工作分区上。
KafkaBroker::new 只记录配置，connect 探测集群，启动时为每个订阅打开一个消费者，关闭时刷出数据。
一条 Kafka 记录在 RustStream 服务中的路径：拉取队列、投递、处理器、应答和提交。
ack、drop、retry 和 retry_after 在 Kafka 上变成什么；Kafka 为每个分区提交一个偏移量，而不是逐条确认记录。
The parts of ruststream-rdkafka a Kafka service uses, one page per component.
With asyncapi the generated document speaks Kafka: the server, the topic behind each channel, the group of each operation.
Each channel reports its topic: the descriptor's for a subscription, the resolved destination for a publish.
A receive operation reports the consumer group its descriptor names, and the client id its config sets.
The server reports bare host:port coordinates and the schema registry, never credentials and never a protocol version.
AvroCodec::registry reads each delivery with its writer schema and frames each value with the id of its subject.
AvroCodec::local pins one schema and writes a bare datum, with no envelope, no registry and no I/O.
resolve_onto reads every delivery onto a reader schema, so Avro fills the fields the writer never wrote from their defaults.
On a broker with schema_registry an Avro datum arrives as JSON, and SchemaFrame writes Avro where the reply's subject holds an Avro schema.
KafkaBroker connects a service to a Kafka cluster; new only records the bootstrap servers, and the runtime connects it at startup.
config and producer_config pass any librdkafka property to every client of the broker or to its producer only.
KafkaError is the one error type of the crate: connect, publish, consume, transactions, the registry and the wire format.
One glob, ruststream_rdkafka::prelude, brings the core prelude, the descriptors, the policies under concept names and the context keys.
SASL and TLS are librdkafka properties set through config; the ssl and ssl-vendored features link the OpenSSL they need.
Shutdown flushes in-flight publishes within flush_timeout, and a publisher used afterwards reports KafkaError::Closed.
Startup probes the cluster within connect_timeout and waits up to assignment_timeout for each group to assign its partitions.
KafkaContext gives a handler the record's topic, partition, offset, timestamp and key, each read as a parameter through Ctx<K>.
A batch handler's context carries the subscription's seek handle; each record's own coordinates travel with the elements.
KafkaPosition names a place in the log: either end, an offset, an offset of one topic, or a timestamp.
A handler moves its running subscription through the SeekHandle key; the seek is local and a rebalance discards it.
start_at opens a subscription at a position on every startup, whatever the group committed.
A prost message rides the byte lanes as itself, and decode_confluent steps over the Confluent envelope with no registry.
KafkaPublish::framed puts the Confluent envelope on every message its policy publishes, with the destination subject's schema id.
ProtobufFrame, added with publish_layer, frames every Protobuf publish of the app that leaves through a slot.
On a broker with schema_registry, framed Protobuf arrives as JSON and leaves framed, with no generated code in the service.
KafkaPublish, Publish in the prelude, is the plain publish policy; every publish waits for the cluster's delivery report.
Durability is the producer's acks; an idempotent producer with Commit::Tracked gives at-least-once from input to output.
The partition-key header becomes the record's native key, so records sharing a key land on one partition, in order.
The partition step pins one record to a partition, ahead of its key and the partitioner.
RoundRobin spreads replies over a fixed partition count, placing only records with no key and no partition.
SchemaRegistry is the Confluent Schema Registry client: it sends nothing until the first lookup, and its clones share one cache.
SchemaCachePolicy bounds the id entries and ages the subject entries, since an id never changes and a subject's latest version moves.
parse_envelope and encode_envelope read and write the Confluent wire format: a zero byte, the schema id, the datum.
schema_registry on the broker and the SchemaFrame layer convert framed payloads to and from plain JSON at the broker's edges.
MissingSubject decides what a codec does when the registry no longer holds its subject: refuse, register the type's schema, or publish unframed.
register, register_json and register_avro put a schema under a subject; warm resolves an existing subject and registers nothing.
RegistryClient is the transport the registry speaks through; HttpRegistryClient is the default, and with_client supplies another.
SchemaFramed wraps a codec such as JsonCodec in the Confluent envelope, so a registry-backed JSON topic is a codec choice.
SchemaPrefetch resolves every registered subject at connect, which keeps the codecs' encode and decode free of I/O.
SubjectStrategy names a subject from the topic, the record name or both, and SchemaFrame::subject pins the subject of one topic.
Another registry stack does the schema work and the byte lanes carry its framed bytes, so no type crosses between the two.
#[derive(Schema)] checks a message type against the newest migration of every subject in schemas/ that declares its record, when the crate compiles.
#[schema(namespace = ..)] compares a type's serde shape with the JSON Schema of its subject, in both directions for an owned subject.
cargo kafka-schema keeps every subject this service owns as numbered migrations in the repository and synchronizes them with the registry.
Commit decides what an ack or a nack does on Kafka, which settles a consumer group by committed position, not per message.
Commit::Auto is librdkafka's timer commit: an ack is advisory, and a retry is not delivered again.
dead_letter names the topic a delivery that reached its cap is republished to, payload and headers as they arrived.
retry_after asks for a later delivery: the runtime republishes a copy to the subscription with its delivery count in a header.
ToSourceTopic sends each retry copy back to the topic its delivery arrived on, for subscriptions over several topics.
Commit::Tracked commits below the lowest unsettled delivery, so a retry comes back and nothing is committed past it.
A topic name in #[subscriber] reads that topic in the broker's default group; a descriptor carries every other setting.
Assignment picks the consumer group's rebalance strategy, eager or cooperative sticky.
A slice handler reads one fetched delivery plus what librdkafka already holds, up to the size the mount site names.
KafkaPartitions reads exactly the partitions it names, joins no group and never rebalances.
KafkaTopic reads one topic in one consumer group, with its start offset, commit mode, assignment and lane key.
KafkaTopics reads a list of topics through one consumer and one group, and each delivery names its topic.
LaneKey decides what workers(n, by_key) keys a lane by: the source partition, or the record key.
A descriptor's config passes any consumer property; one the commit mode owns is refused at startup, naming the property.
KafkaTopicPattern reads every topic a librdkafka regex starting with ^ matches, those created later included.
schema(namespace) on a descriptor checks at startup that the topic's registry subjects exist and declare records of that namespace.
StartOffset says where a group starts on a partition with no committed offset: committed reset, earliest or latest.
TestApp::start connects KafkaBroker to an in-process cluster with topics, groups, offsets and transactions.
TestApp::start_live runs the same test body against a running Kafka, for what only a cluster has.
transactional_id makes the publish policy transactional: publishes between begin and commit become visible together, or not at all.
KafkaEosPublish commits consumed offsets inside the producer's transaction, so positions move atomically with the records published.
EosPipeline::publish sends a record into the open window by hand, with the source coordinates the Source key gives.
EosReplies joins every reply to the pipeline's open window, paired with its delivery's consumed offset.
per_partition gives each source partition its own transactional publisher, so a worker pool runs independent transactions.
选择 ack 和 nack 在 Kafka 上提交什么：librdkafka 自己的提交、Commit::Tracked 下精确的至少一次，以及逐个元素结算的批。

在消费者组中读取主题，用并行的工作分区保持每个键的顺序，并按键、按编号或轮流把记录放到分区上。
把 Kafka 服务连接到生产集群：SASL 与 TLS、生产者持久性、超时、按订阅覆盖的配置，以及对配置的测试。

ruststream-rdkafka 是 RustStream 的 Apache Kafka Broker， 基于 rust-rdkafka 和 librdkafka 构建。这些指南带你把一个 Kafka 服务从安装一路推进到生产环境。 从快速开始读起。
本节用图说明 Kafka 如何工作，ruststream-rdkafka 在 Kafka 与 RustStream 运行时之间处于什么位置，以及这给服务带来的开销。
ruststream-rdkafka 在每条消息上的开销：与裸 rdkafka 客户端对照的吞吐量，以及它自身代码的指令数和内存分配次数。

第一张图在真实的 Kafka Broker 上把同一个场景用三种方式运行。裸客户端 直接驱动一个 librdkafka 消费者。Broker crate 用一个自己的循环驱动本 crate 的订阅，上面没有运行时。RustStream 是用户写的服务：应用里的一个 #[subscriber] 处理器。第一项差值是本 crate 比它所封装的客户端多付出的开销，第二项是运行时在其上增加的开销。 每个循环画成一条横条，从最佳一轮延伸到最慢的一轮，圆点标出最佳一轮，缺口标出中位一轮。坐标轴的零点是裸客户端的最佳一轮，圆点在零点右侧表示更慢。空心圆点表示该循环与裸客户端的差异小于各轮的波动范围。图表下方的表格列出最佳一轮，括号里是中位数。 两个场景的区别在于 ack 的含义。在自动提交下，librdkafka 在交出记录时就存储了偏移量，ack 只起建议作用。在 Commit::Tracked 下，每次 ack 都会存储一个偏移量，结算一页用图说明了这一点。

第二张图统计一条消息在服务线程上的开销：稳态下 callgrind 测得的指令数和 DHAT 测得的内存分配次数。每个场景都是一个基于 KafkaBroker、连接同一个 Broker 的服务。计数包括框架的分发、本 crate 的代码，以及在该线程上发起的 librdkafka 调用。拉取、组协议、生产和投递报告运行在 librdkafka 自己的线程上，不计入。冷启动 是启动服务、加入组并取得第一条记录一次性付出的开销。

ruststream-rdkafka 如何测量自己：三个循环、在真实 Broker 上的运行、受 Broker 限制的判定计算，以及代码计数。流程就是框架自己的流程（RustStream 方法论），本页说明它在 Kafka 上是什么样子。

一个进程把每个场景跑三遍，作为三个循环，它们只有一处不同：承载记录的是什么。 裸客户端。 一个 rdkafka StreamConsumer，直接驱动：接收、解码、存储偏移量。 Broker crate。 本 crate，上面什么也没有：Broker 建立连接，主题描述符打开一个订阅，一个循环从它的流中取出投递、解码并 ack。 RustStream。 用户写的服务：一个 #[subscriber] 处理器及其外围的应用。 其余一切在三个循环中都相同：消费者属性、消费者组、提交模式、ack 的位置、解码成同一个结构体、载荷字节、带四个工作线程的 tokio 运行时，以及二进制程序。 消息体是 512 字节的 JSON。它解码成一个包含两个整数字段的结构体，因此解码不做内存分配，数字反映的是本 crate，而不是 JSON 解析器。

每次运行使用新的主题和新的消费者组。 主题只有一个分区，运行结束后删除，因此一次运行永远看不到之前的运行留下的东西。 消费者先加入。 生产者使用自己的客户端，在集群报告出组的成员之后才开始。 在三个循环中，计时窗口都从第一次投递开始，到最后一次投递解码完成时结束。 加入组和创建主题都在窗口之外。 消息条数来自一次探测，它测量裸循环的速率，因此在任何机器上，测量的运行都至少持续五秒。 各循环交替进行：裸、crate、RustStream，共三轮。每个循环报告它最佳、中位和最差的一轮。 当裸客户端在运行中一直在等套接字时，该行标为 受 Broker 限制。这是算出来的：一次探测为一个元数据请求及其应答计时，第二次探测统计 librdkafka 每次投递发送的请求数，二者之积达到每条消息测得时间的一半时，该行就被标记。往返时间与机器信息一起公布，因此这个计算可以核对。

开销图的每个场景都是用户写的服务，基于 KafkaBroker，连接同一个 Broker，构建时不带 testing 特性。一个消费者组读取一个只有一个分区的主题，另一个线程在测量区间打开之前把主题填满。 指令数来自 callgrind，内存分配来自 DHAT。一个场景依次在一次投递、1000 次、2000 次上运行。后两次之差是一条消息的稳态开销，单次投递就是冷启动。 Broker 是真实的，所以同一个二进制程序每次运行的计数都会变动：服务线程有多少次发现队列为空并等待，取决于时序。三次运行中，消费场景和批场景的结果相差在万分之一以内，应答场景变动了 2.3%。因此，与保存的基线对照时，某个场景的指令数多出百分之五就算失败，而核心的上限是百分之二。内存分配在每次运行中都受每个场景声明的下限约束。

just bench 这条命令按 docker-compose.test.yml 启动测试环境，运行两个对照场景，停止测试环境，并重写 docs/benchmarks/results.json。它大约需要十五分钟，并且需要独占机器。它会清空 RUSTFLAGS，因此二进制程序不会绑定到构建它的 CPU 上。两条命令都按发布版本的方式构建基准测试，跨 crate 启用完整的链接时优化（fat LTO），因此这些数字描述的正是服务实际使用的代码。 just bench-code 代码计数需要一两分钟，并且需要 valgrind。在 main 上运行 just bench-code --save-baseline=main 记录基线，在分支上运行 just bench-code --baseline=main 与它对照。
ruststream-rdkafka 的基准测试数字测的是什么，以及不能从中得出哪些结论。

同一行中的三个循环可以互相比较，因为它们在同一个进程中、交替地、对着同一个 Broker 运行。一行不能与另一个 Broker crate 公布的行比较：各种传输在每条消息上做的工作不同。 Broker 运行在同一台机器上，走回环接口。没有网络延迟，同样的每条消息开销在时间中所占的比例，比面对跨网络的集群时更大。应把该百分比读作已部署服务所付代价的上界。 受 Broker 限制 的行表示裸客户端在运行的大部分时间里都在等套接字。本 crate 和运行时的工作于是发生在这段等待之内，测出的差异接近零。这是开销的下界，而不是对它的测量。
指令计数包含本 crate 的代码、它上面的运行时，以及在服务线程上发起的 librdkafka 调用。由于 Broker 是真实的，它在各次运行之间会有少许变动。同样的计数在缓存未命中处要花更多时间，因此计数不等于时间。 每个数字都是稳态，即 1000 次投递的运行与 2000 次投递的运行之差。启动服务、加入组以及它们背后的首批内存分配属于冷启动，只付一次。

一行就是一个消费者读取一个只有一个分区的主题，消息体很小，集群只有一个节点。它测量的是一次投递在本 crate 内部的开销，而不是 Kafka 能承载多少。 多分区的主题、一组工作分区和事务流水线各自回答不同的问题，这个对照不测量其中任何一个。代码图在同一测试环境上统计批处理器和应答。 这些数字是一台机器在某一天的快照，构建信息记录在旁边。它们在一台只做这次运行的机器上手动重新测量：它们显示的差异小于共享机器的噪声。

Kafka 主题是一组分区，每个分区都是按偏移量编号的有序记录日志，每个消费者组都读取它的全部内容。 生产者向一个主题的各个分区追加记录，两个消费者组各自读取整个主题追加读取每条记录读取每条记录主题 orders组 billing组 audit生产者键决定分区P0012345P10123P201234成员 1：P0、P1成员 2：P2成员 1：P0、P1、P2每个组按分区提交自己的偏移量：也就是它继续读取的那条记录 以文字阅读本图 主题 orders: P0; 0; 1; 2; 3; 4; 5; P1; 0; 1; 2; 3; P2; 0; 1; 2; 3; 4 组 billing: 成员 1：P0、P1; 成员 2：P2 组 audit: 成员 1： P0、P1、P2 生产者 键决定分区 → 主题 orders: 追加 主题 orders → 组 billing: 读取每条记录 主题 orders → 组 audit: 读取每条记录 每个组按分区提交自己的偏移量： 也就是它继续读取的那条记录 生产者把一条记录追加到主题的一个分区。带键的记录进入其键的哈希所对应的分区，因此同一个键的记录保持顺序。不带键的记录由生产者的分区器决定去向。 每个分区从零开始给记录编号，它的偏移量与其他分区的偏移量各自增长。顺序只在分区内部成立，在其他任何地方都不成立。记录一直留在日志里，直到保留策略删除它，不管有没有人读过。 消费者组把主题的每条记录读一次。组把每个分区交给它的一个成员，于是成员们分担工作。第二个组对每条记录读取属于自己的一份，两个组互不影响。 组读到了哪里，就是每个分区一个数字：它已提交的偏移量，也就是它继续读取的那条记录。Kafka 不保存逐条记录的确认。 这一模型就是 Apache Kafka 自己的模型（概念与术语）。组如何分担分区，见消费者组；客户端如何读取和提交，见消费者。

librdkafka 消费者在自己的线程上预先拉取，每次轮询交出一条记录，并按计时器提交已存储的偏移量。 librdkafka 消费者：拉取线程、本地队列、应用的轮询、偏移量存储和提交计时器记录交出时或稍后读取提交librdkafka 线程应用Kafka 集群分区 leader、组协调者拉取已分配的分区本地队列预先拉取自动提交按计时器，每 5 秒轮询下一条记录处理这条记录偏移量存储在内存中，每个分区一个位置 以文字阅读本图 librdkafka 线程: 拉取 已分配的分区; 本地队列 预先拉取; 自动提交 按计时器， 每 5 秒 应用: 轮询 下一条记录; 处理 这条记录; 偏移量存储 在内存中， 每个分区 一个位置 Kafka 集群 分区 leader、组协调者 → 拉取 已分配的分区: 记录 拉取 已分配的分区 → 本地队列 预先拉取 本地队列 预先拉取 → 轮询 下一条记录 轮询 下一条记录 → 处理 这条记录 轮询 下一条记录 → 偏移量存储 在内存中， 每个分区 一个位置: 交出时 处理 这条记录 → 偏移量存储 在内存中， 每个分区 一个位置: 或稍后 偏移量存储 在内存中， 每个分区 一个位置 → 自动提交 按计时器， 每 5 秒: 读取 自动提交 按计时器， 每 5 秒 → Kafka 集群 分区 leader、组协调者: 提交 librdkafka 在应用请求之前，就把已分配分区的记录拉取到本地队列中。queued.max.messages.kbytes（64 MiB）限制这个队列的大小。队列满时，对某个分区的拉取暂停 fetch.queue.backoff.ms（一秒）。 一次轮询从队列中取出下一条记录。rust-rdkafka 的 StreamConsumer 通过 recv 完成这一步，这是一个取消安全的异步调用。 偏移量存储是每个分区在内存中的一个位置。默认情况下（enable.auto.offset.store），轮询在应用处理记录之前，就存储它交出的那条记录的偏移量。虚线箭头是另一种方式：应用关闭自动存储，在记录处理完之后再存储偏移量。 enable.auto.commit 开启时，计时器每隔 auto.commit.interval.ms（五秒）提交一次已存储的位置，消费者关闭时再提交一次。崩溃会丢失上次提交之后已处理的进度，这部分记录会被再读一遍。在默认的存储方式下，交出时已存储、尚未处理的记录在崩溃后会被跳过。 行为和默认值来自 librdkafka（偏移量管理、配置）。

消费者组把每个分区交给一个成员；成员加入或离开时，分区通过再均衡转移。 一次再均衡：成员加入，协调者把一个分区转给它，它从已提交的偏移量继续读取成员 1协调者成员 2加入撤销分配读取P0、P1、P2加入组再均衡：新的分配P2 被撤销读取P0、P1从已提交的偏移量读取P2停止心跳超过 session.timeout.ms 的成员离开组，它的分区以同样方式转移 以文字阅读本图 成员 1: 读取 P0、P1、P2; P2 被 撤销; 读取 P0、P1 协调者: 再均衡： 新的 分配; 停止心跳超过 session.timeout.ms 的成员 离开组，它的分区以同样方式转移 成员 2: 加入 组; 从已提交的 偏移量读取 P2 加入 组 → 再均衡： 新的 分配: 加入 再均衡： 新的 分配 → P2 被 撤销: 撤销 P2 被 撤销 → 读取 P0、P1 再均衡： 新的 分配 → 从已提交的 偏移量读取 P2: 分配 组协调者是集群中的一个 Broker。成员加入或离开时，它发起再均衡，组就新的分配达成一致。从一个成员拿走的分区在那里被撤销，并分配给另一个成员，后者从组已提交的偏移量继续读取。前一个成员在最后一次提交之后做的工作，会被第二个成员再读一遍。组从未提交过的分区从 auto.offset.reset 指定的位置开始：默认是日志末尾。 停止发送心跳超过 session.timeout.ms（librdkafka 中为 45 秒）的成员会被移出组。超过 max.poll.interval.ms（5 分钟）没有取新记录的成员也会离开组。 partition.assignment.strategy 决定再均衡如何转移分区。急切（eager）策略 range 和 roundrobin（librdkafka 的默认值是两者都用，range 在前）会撤销全部分区再重新分配。cooperative-sticky 只转移更换所有者的分区，其余分区在再均衡期间照常流动（KIP-429）。两类策略不能在同一个组内混用。 消费者也可以按名称直接获取分区，而不加入组协议。这样它永远不会再均衡，也没有任何东西会转移它的分区。 默认值来自 librdkafka（配置、消费者组）。

Kafka 事务让写入多个分区的记录和已消费的偏移量一起变得可见，或者全都不可见。 消费-转换-生产事务：记录和已消费的偏移量一起提交，或者中止时一并丢弃写入标记出错时开始在事务生产者上生产记录到任意分区发送已消费的偏移量连同组的元数据提交事务read_committed 读取者看到这些记录，偏移量算作已提交中止：记录被丢弃，偏移量不动，输入被再读一遍一个事务 id 属于一个存活的生产者：再次初始化它会隔离先前那个 以文字阅读本图 开始 在事务生产者上 → 生产 记录到任意分区 生产 记录到任意分区 → 发送已消费的偏移量 连同组的元数据 发送已消费的偏移量 连同组的元数据 → 提交 事务 提交 事务 → read_committed 读取者 看到这些记录， 偏移量算作已提交: 写入标记 发送已消费的偏移量 连同组的元数据 → 中止： 记录被丢弃， 偏移量不动， 输入被 再读一遍: 出错时 一个事务 id 属于一个存活的生产者： 再次初始化它会隔离先前那个 事务生产者以它的 transactional.id 命名。它一次运行一个事务。事务中生产的记录会立即落入日志，提交时写入的标记使它们变得可见。 处于 read_committed 隔离级别（librdkafka 的默认值）的读取者，只在提交之后才看到事务的记录，中止之后则永远看不到。处于 read_uncommitted 的读取者在记录写入时就能看到它们。 已消费的偏移量可以加入事务。这样，输入的位置恰好在输出变得可见时移动，这就是 KIP-447 的消费-转换-生产模式。中止会让偏移量留在原处，于是输入被再读一遍，进入新的事务。 打开时间超过 transaction.timeout.ms（一分钟）的事务会被协调者中止。用一个已在使用的 id 启动的生产者会隔离（fence）先前的那个：先前那个生产者的下一次调用会失败。 默认值和隔离规则来自 librdkafka（事务生产者、配置）。

一个订阅通过一个消费者读取它的全部分区；workers(n, by_key) 把记录分到按分区划分的工作分区上。 一个订阅的分发：三个分区、一个消费者、一个流，以及按分区划分的两个工作分区已拉取的记录一次一条分区 0分区 1分区 2订阅的消费者组分配给它的全部分区KafkaSubscriber 流一次一条记录workers(2, by_key)工作分区 = 分区的哈希工作分区 1分区 0 和 2，各自有序工作分区 2分区 1，有序在 LaneKey::RecordKey 下，工作分区按记录键划分：一个分区分散到多个工作分区，每个键内部有序 以文字阅读本图 分区 0 → 订阅的消费者 组分配给它的全部分区 分区 1 → 订阅的消费者 组分配给它的全部分区 分区 2 → 订阅的消费者 组分配给它的全部分区 订阅的消费者 组分配给它的全部分区 → KafkaSubscriber 流 一次一条记录: 已拉取的记录 KafkaSubscriber 流 一次一条记录 → workers(2, by_key) 工作分区 = 分区的哈希: 一次一条 workers(2, by_key) 工作分区 = 分区的哈希 → 工作分区 1 分区 0 和 2， 各自有序 workers(2, by_key) 工作分区 = 分区的哈希 → 工作分区 2 分区 1，有序 在 LaneKey::RecordKey 下，工作分区按记录键划分： 一个分区分散到多个工作分区，每个键内部有序 订阅的流一次产出一条记录，不管它来自哪个分区。不用 workers 时，一个循环依次为每条记录运行处理器，因此每个分区都保持顺序，也没有任何东西并行运行。 workers(n, by_key) 运行 n 个工作分区。记录进入其键的哈希所对应的工作分区，每个工作分区按顺序运行自己的记录。键默认是记录所在的分区（LaneKey::Partition），因此一个分区绝不会分散到两个工作分区上，Kafka 的顺序得以保持。工作分区少于分区时，每个工作分区服务多个分区。 LaneKey::RecordKey 改为按记录键划分工作分区。同一个键的记录保持顺序，一个分区里的不同键并行运行。没有键的记录也就没有分区键，这样的记录轮流分配到各个工作分区。 并行的工作分区发来的 ack 是乱序到达的。在 Commit::Tracked 下，已提交的偏移量仍然绝不会越过尚未结算的记录，结算一页用图说明了这一点。 批处理器接收一条记录，以及 librdkafka 已经拉取的其余记录，最多到挂载处指定的大小，因此一个批往往小于这个大小。

KafkaBroker::new 只记录配置，connect 探测集群，启动时为每个订阅打开一个消费者，关闭时刷出数据。 Broker 的三个状态作为类型，以及每次转换在 Kafka 上做什么connect(self)shutdown(self)Broker在 Kafka 上KafkaBroker::new(servers)ConnectedKafkaBrokerClosedKafkaBrokerunflushed_records()只记录配置，无 I/O元数据探测，在 connect_timeout 内每个订阅：一个消费者，入组并分到它的分区第一次发布打开生产者在 flush_timeout内刷出在途的记录比连接活得更久的发布者返回 KafkaError::Closed，绝不默默成功 以文字阅读本图 Broker: KafkaBroker::new (servers); ConnectedKafkaBroker; ClosedKafkaBroker unflushed_records() 在 Kafka 上: 只记录配置， 无 I/O; 元数据探测， 在 connect_timeout 内; 每个订阅： 一个消费者，入组 并分到它的分区; 第一次发布 打开生产者; 在 flush_timeout 内刷出在途 的记录 KafkaBroker::new (servers) → ConnectedKafkaBroker: connect(self) ConnectedKafkaBroker → ClosedKafkaBroker unflushed_records(): shutdown(self) 只记录配置， 无 I/O → 元数据探测， 在 connect_timeout 内 元数据探测， 在 connect_timeout 内 → 每个订阅： 一个消费者，入组 并分到它的分区 每个订阅： 一个消费者，入组 并分到它的分区 → 第一次发布 打开生产者 第一次发布 打开生产者 → 在 flush_timeout 内刷出在途 的记录 比连接活得更久的发布者 返回 KafkaError::Closed，绝不默默成功 new 不做任何 I/O，所以服务的构建函数保持同步。运行时在应用启动时连接 Broker。connect 用一个由生产者设置构建的短命客户端获取集群的元数据，时限为 connect_timeout（30 秒）。集群不可达，或者 librdkafka 拒绝某个生产者属性，启动就会失败。 每个订阅的描述符针对已连接的 Broker 解析一次。加入消费者组的订阅打开它的消费者，并等待组给它分配分区、每个分区的起点都已知，最长等待 assignment_timeout（一分钟）。在运行时开始读取之前，消费者一直响应组，因此再均衡不会等它。订阅没有指定组，而 Broker 又没有 default_group 时，启动就会失败。 只消费的服务不运行生产者。第一次发布时才打开共用的那个生产者。 关闭先把连接标为已关闭，然后在 flush_timeout（30 秒）内刷出生产者仍持有的数据。ClosedKafkaBroker 报告刷出后遗留的记录。订阅被丢弃时，它的消费者随之关闭：消费者离开组，并且除非订阅是事务性的，还会在离开时提交已存储的位置。

一条 Kafka 记录在 RustStream 服务中的路径：拉取队列、投递、处理器、应答和提交。 一条需要应答的 Kafka 记录的路径：从 librdkafka 的拉取队列到它已提交的偏移量librdkafka 拉取队列预先拉取的记录KafkaMessage记录留在拉取缓冲区分发一个循环，或每个键一个工作分区解码直接从缓冲区读取订阅者的处理器#[subscriber] 下的 async fn应答编码进循环的缓冲区KafkaPublisher等待投递报告结算由 Commit 模式决定提交已存储的偏移量 以文字阅读本图 librdkafka 拉取队列 预先拉取的记录 → KafkaMessage 记录留在拉取缓冲区 KafkaMessage 记录留在拉取缓冲区 → 分发 一个循环，或每个键一个工作分区 分发 一个循环，或每个键一个工作分区 → 解码 直接从缓冲区读取 解码 直接从缓冲区读取 → 订阅者的处理器 #[subscriber] 下的 async fn 订阅者的处理器 #[subscriber] 下的 async fn → 应答 编码进循环的缓冲区 应答 编码进循环的缓冲区 → KafkaPublisher 等待投递报告 KafkaPublisher 等待投递报告 → 结算 由 Commit 模式决定 结算 由 Commit 模式决定 → 提交 已存储的偏移量 librdkafka 已经拉取的记录无需等待即可取出。KafkaMessage 把记录留在 librdkafka 放置它的位置，同时持有对拥有该缓冲区的消费者的一个引用计数。消息体、键和消息头都从拉取缓冲区读取，不做复制，消息头只在有人请求时才转换。只要还有投递持有某个消费者的记录，该消费者就保持打开。 唯一被复制的记录，是等待中的流自己取到的那一条：队列为空时，等待所返回的记录会被复制出来。 处理器的应答编码进分发循环复用的缓冲区。发布者把这些字节借给 librdkafka，librdkafka 把它们复制进自己的队列，集群确认这条记录之后，发布才返回。应答发布失败时，这次投递以重试的方式结算。 投递在应答之后结算。这对已提交的偏移量有什么影响，取决于订阅的 Commit 模式，结算一页用图说明了这一点。

ack、drop、retry 和 retry_after 在 Kafka 上变成什么。Kafka 为每个分区提交一个偏移量，而不是逐条确认记录。 单个分区上的 Commit::Tracked：已存储的位置停在尚未结算的最低投递之下存储于自动提交一个分区，偏移量按投递顺序10已结算11已结算12运行中13已结算14已结算15运行中已存储的位置：11低于运行中的最低投递已提交的偏移量：12组从这条记录继续读取12 结算后，位置移到 14：15 仍在运行 以文字阅读本图 已存储的位置：11 低于运行中的 最低投递 → 11 已结算: 存储于 已存储的位置：11 低于运行中的 最低投递 → 已提交的偏移量：12 组从这条记录 继续读取: 自动提交 一个分区，偏移量按投递顺序 10 已结算 12 运行中 13 已结算 14 已结算 15 运行中 12 结算后， 位置移到 14： 15 仍在 运行 Kafka 为每个分区和组保存一个已提交的偏移量。订阅的 Commit 模式决定处理器的结果如何到达那里。 在 Commit::Tracked 下，本 crate 关闭 librdkafka 的自动偏移量存储，并记录它投递的每个偏移量。每次结算都把位置存储在仍在运行的最低投递之下，没有运行中的投递时，则存储已投递的最高偏移量。并行工作分区发来的 ack 可以按任意顺序到达，已存储的位置绝不会越过未完成的工作。消费者永远收不到的偏移量，比如事务标记或被压缩掉的记录，不会阻挡它。librdkafka 的计时器照常提交已存储的位置。 结果 Commit::Auto（默认） Commit::Tracked Commit::Transactional ack 什么也不做：librdkafka 在交出记录时就已存储偏移量 该偏移量结算，已存储的位置上移 该偏移量结算；流水线在下一个窗口提交它 drop 什么也不做，与 ack 相同 该偏移量结算，与 ack 相同 该偏移量结算，与 ack 相同 retry() 被拒绝（AckError::Unsupported）并记录日志：没有任何东西能把记录送回来 记录在接下来拉取的内容之前再次投递，位置等待它 当前打开的窗口无法提交：它中止，其中的记录被重新读取 再均衡或 seek 移动了某个分区时，该分区的跟踪状态会被丢弃。对移动之前读到的投递进行结算不会改变任何东西，因为该分区的下一个读取者无论如何都从已提交的偏移量开始。 在 Commit::Transactional 下，消费者自己不提交任何东西。同一 id 的 EosPipeline 每隔 commit_interval（100 毫秒）把已结算的位置加入它的生产者事务，于是已消费的偏移量和已发布的记录同时变得可见，Kafka 事务一页用图说明了这一点。

Kafka 上的一次重试：尝试上限决定把副本发到主题、发到死信主题，还是丢弃已处理重试低于上限到达上限一条记录x-ruststream-retry-count 说明这是第几次尝试处理器返回retry_after(delay)，或在有声明时返回 retry()max_attempts：这次尝试是否低于上限？低于上限：原记录结算，副本发往主题到达上限：副本发往死信主题到达上限，没有死信：记录结算，不发副本副本是一条新记录，位于其分区的末尾延迟的副本保存在进程中：计时器触发前崩溃就会丢失它 以文字阅读本图 一条记录 x-ruststream-retry-count 说明这是第几次尝试 → 处理器返回 retry_after(delay)，或在有声明时返回 retry(): 已处理 处理器返回 retry_after(delay)，或在有声明时返回 retry() → max_attempts：这次尝试是否低于上限？: 重试 max_attempts：这次尝试是否低于上限？ → 低于上限： 原记录 结算，副本 发往主题: 低于上限 max_attempts：这次尝试是否低于上限？ → 到达上限： 副本发往 死信 主题: 到达上限 max_attempts：这次尝试是否低于上限？ → 到达上限， 没有死信： 记录结算， 不发副本 低于上限： 原记录 结算，副本 发往主题 → 副本是一条新记录， 位于其分区的末尾 延迟的副本保存在进程中： 计时器触发前崩溃就会丢失它 Kafka 既不扣留记录，也不统计投递次数，所以这两件事都由运行时来做。retry_after 结果，以及声明了 max_attempts 或死信主题的注册上的 retry()，在每种提交模式下都走这条路径。尝试次数随副本的 x-ruststream-retry-count 消息头传递，第一次投递算作一次。 副本发往描述符报告的地址。KafkaTopic 订阅报告它自己的主题。KafkaTopics 或 KafkaPartitions 订阅读取的是一个单次发布到达不了的集合，所以它的注册要指定目的地，否则应用拒绝启动。 副本保留记录的键，因此它再次落到该键的分区上，排在此后写入的记录之后。读取该主题的每个消费者组都会收到副本，而不只是发起重试的那个组。
The parts of ruststream-rdkafka a Kafka service uses, one page per component: the broker (KafkaBroker), its subscriptions, its publish policies and the in-process transport a TestApp test runs on.

With the asyncapi feature the generated document speaks Kafka: the server, the topic behind each channel, the group of each operation. The core builds the AsyncAPI document from the app, before anything connects. This crate adds the specification's kafka binding, version 0.5.0, to the parts it knows about. A server reports the cluster's coordinates and its schema registry. A channel reports the topic behind it. A receive operation reports the consumer group it reads in. Everything comes from the service's own declarations: the broker, the descriptors and the destinations the mount sites resolved. The document is published and shared, so no binding carries a credential. The binary #[ruststream::app] writes prints the document with asyncapi gen.

The dependency line: ruststream-rdkafka = { version = "0.7", features = ["asyncapi"] } The service registers its broker under the label kafka, the key of its server in the document. cargo run --example kafka_asyncapi --features asyncapi,schema-registry -- asyncapi gen prints the document. Macros Manual examples/kafka_asyncapi.rs fn service(broker: KafkaBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "1.0.0")).with_broker_labeled("kafka", broker, |b| { b.include(confirm); b.include(audit); b.include(ledger); }) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { let password = env::var("KAFKA_PASSWORD").unwrap_or_default(); service(broker(&password)) } examples/manual/kafka_asyncapi.rs fn service(broker: KafkaBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "1.0.0")).with_broker_labeled("kafka", broker, |b| { let confirm = subscriber("orders", Confirm).map_source(|_| orders()); b.include(confirm.reply().to("confirmations").build()); b.include( subscriber("audit", Audit) .map_source(|_| audit_topics()) .build(), ); b.include( subscriber("ledger", Ledger) .map_source(|_| ledger_partitions()) .build(), ); }) } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { let password = env::var("KAFKA_PASSWORD").unwrap_or_default(); service(broker(&password)) }

Each channel reports its topic: the descriptor's for a subscription, the resolved destination for a publish. The channel binding has one field, topic. A subscription by name, a KafkaTopic and a KafkaPartitions reader each report the one topic they read. A KafkaTopics set or pattern reads several topics, so its channel carries no binding. A channel the service publishes to reports the topic the mount site resolved. That is a reply("dest") clause, a reply type's #[outgoing(name)], the name of a slot entry, or a declared dead-letter topic. A publish policy holds producer settings and no topic, so the policy itself adds nothing to the channel.

The channels orders and ledger report the topics their descriptors read, and confirmations the topic the reply clause names. The channel of the audit and audit.eu set reports none. Macros Manual examples/kafka_asyncapi.rs #[subscriber( KafkaTopic::new("orders") .group("orders-svc") .config("client.id", "orders-reader"), reply("confirmations") )] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Confirmation { Confirmation { id: order.id } } #[subscriber(KafkaTopics::new(["audit", "audit.eu"]).group("audit-svc"))] async fn audit(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "audited"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[subscriber(KafkaPartitions::new("ledger", [0, 1]))] async fn ledger(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "booked"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/kafka_asyncapi.rs /// The topic `orders`, read in the group `orders-svc` by the client `orders-reader`. fn orders() -> KafkaTopic { KafkaTopic::new("orders") .group("orders-svc") .config("client.id", "orders-reader") } /// Both audit topics, through one consumer in the group `audit-svc`. fn audit_topics() -> KafkaTopics { KafkaTopics::new(["audit", "audit.eu"]).group("audit-svc") } /// The first two partitions of `ledger`, read apart from any group. fn ledger_partitions() -> KafkaPartitions { KafkaPartitions::new("ledger", [0, 1]) }

A receive operation reports the consumer group its descriptor names, and the client id its config sets. The operation binding carries groupId and clientId, each as a one-value schema. groupId is the group the descriptor names, such as KafkaTopic::group. The document is built before the broker connects, from the descriptor alone, so the broker's default_group does not appear. clientId appears when the descriptor's config sets client.id. An operation with neither carries no binding.

The operation receive_orders reports the group orders-svc and the client id orders-reader. Macros Manual examples/kafka_asyncapi.rs #[subscriber( KafkaTopic::new("orders") .group("orders-svc") .config("client.id", "orders-reader"), reply("confirmations") )] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Confirmation { Confirmation { id: order.id } } examples/manual/kafka_asyncapi.rs /// The topic `orders`, read in the group `orders-svc` by the client `orders-reader`. fn orders() -> KafkaTopic { KafkaTopic::new("orders") .group("orders-svc") .config("client.id", "orders-reader") }

The server reports bare host:port coordinates and the schema registry, never credentials and never a protocol version. A broker registered with with_broker_labeled is a server of the document, under its label. Its host is the bootstrap servers, joined with commas. A PLAINTEXT:// or SASL_SSL:// prefix and any user info an address carries stay out of it. The protocol is kafka. protocolVersion stays out: a Kafka client and the cluster agree on a version per request type, so no one number describes what clients speak. A broker with a SchemaRegistry adds the server binding. schemaRegistryUrl is the registry's address without user info, and schemaRegistryVendor is confluent, the envelope this crate writes. The SASL password and the registry's basic-auth credentials stay out of the document.

The broker reaches two brokers over SASL_SSL and a registry with basic auth. Its server in the document is kafka-1.internal:9093,kafka-2.internal:9093 with the registry https://registry.internal:8081. AvroCodec::registry reads each delivery with its writer schema and frames each value with the id of its subject. AvroCodec is a codec, so a handler on it takes and returns ordinary serde structs. A model derives AvroSchema from apache-avro, which the crate re-exports as avro::AvroSchema. The codec is built from a SchemaPrefetch, and the same prefetch is attached to the broker with KafkaBroker::schema_prefetch. The codec itself is synchronous and reads only the prefetch's cache, so its encode and decode reach no network. Decoding needs no registration. The envelope of each delivery names the writer schema, the prefetch resolves it before the decode, and the codec reads the datum with it. One codec therefore decodes every record type that arrives on its topics. register::<T>(subject) is the publish side: values of T are framed with the id of subject. The codec finds the subject by the name serde gives the value's type. A value of a type that no one registered fails its publish, and the error names the type and lists the registered ones. Two registered types with one serde name stop the app at startup. The codec named with with_broker_codec decodes the deliveries of its scope. A reply names its codec at its own position, .out_reply(policy).codec(codec); a reply without one is encoded with the default codec. The codec and the transcode are alternatives on one broker: a broker with schema_registry hands every subscription plain JSON.

// Registration is the publish side: the subject a type's values are framed under. let codec = AvroCodec::registry(&prefetch).register::<Receipt>("delivery-receipts-value"); let broker = KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]) .default_group("deliveries-svc") .schema_prefetch(prefetch); AvroCodec::local pins one schema and writes a bare datum, with no envelope, no registry and no I/O. The schema passed in is the one the wire carries: T::get_schema() when the model defines it, or a parsed .avsc file when the schema text is the source of truth. Every message is written and read with that schema, so producers and consumers of the topic agree on it outside the service. local returns an error when the schema refers to a name it does not define. The codec registers nothing; register belongs to the registry form. avro::encode and avro::decode are the same conversion as free functions, for a tool that works on datum bytes outside an app. Both use the type's own schema.

Macros Manual examples/kafka_avro_local.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, AvroSchema)] struct Reading { sensor: String, celsius: f64, } #[subscriber("readings")] async fn record(reading: &Reading) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(reading.sensor, reading.celsius, "reading recorded"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { // The schema the wire carries, pinned here; nothing reaches a registry. let codec = AvroCodec::local(Reading::get_schema()).expect("a derived schema resolves"); let broker = KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("readings-svc"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("readings", "0.1.0")).with_broker_codec(broker, codec, |b| { b.include(record); }) } examples/manual/kafka_avro_local.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, AvroSchema, JsonSchema)] struct Reading { sensor: String, celsius: f64, } /// The definition `#[subscriber("readings")]` would have minted. struct Record; impl Handle<Reading> for Record { fn handle( &self, reading: &Reading, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(reading.sensor, reading.celsius, "reading recorded"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { // The schema the wire carries, pinned here; nothing reaches a registry. let codec = AvroCodec::local(Reading::get_schema()).expect("a derived schema resolves"); let broker = KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("readings-svc"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("readings", "0.1.0")).with_broker_codec(broker, codec, |b| { b.include(subscriber("readings", Record).build()); }) } // What `#[ruststream::app]` writes: the command line on a multi-threaded Tokio runtime. fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) }

resolve_onto reads every delivery onto a reader schema, so Avro fills the fields the writer never wrote from their defaults. A datum read with its writer schema yields what the writer wrote. A consumer whose model has moved ahead of its producers names its own schema as the reader schema, and Avro's schema resolution fills each missing field from the default that schema declares. The model declares a default with #[avro(default = "..")], whose value is JSON. A field with no default that the writer never wrote fails the decode. The reader schema applies to decoding only; a publish still writes the schema the wire carries. On a local codec the pair is checked when the codec is built, so a reader schema that cannot resolve against the writer schema is an error at startup. On a registry codec the writer schemas arrive with the deliveries, so a pair that cannot resolve fails the decode that meets it. A codec carrying a reader schema reads one type, so a handler that needs one mounts it in a Router with with_codec, and the scope's codec serves the other handlers.

On a broker with schema_registry an Avro datum arrives as JSON, and SchemaFrame writes Avro where the reply's subject holds an Avro schema. The handler and its models stay on the default JSON codec and carry no Avro type. On the way in, the subscription reads the envelope, resolves the writer schema by its id and rewrites the payload as a JSON document. On the way out, the layer resolves the subject of the destination topic, {topic}-value, and writes the JSON payload as an Avro datum of that subject's schema, inside the envelope. The reply's model derives AvroSchema only to register its subject at startup with register_avro. The flow is the same as the JSON transcode; the subject's schema type decides the format on the wire. The transcode is the compatibility path for a service that keeps plain serde models on a registry-backed topic. Each message takes a hop through JSON. A datum is read with its writer schema alone, so a field the writer never wrote has no default to take; the codec with resolve_onto is the path that resolves schemas. An Avro type that JSON has no form for does not pass through the transcode.

KafkaBroker connects a service to a Kafka cluster; new only records the bootstrap servers, and the runtime connects it at startup. KafkaBroker::new takes the bootstrap servers, each a host or host:port the client starts from. It does no I/O, so the whole service fits the synchronous #[ruststream::app] builder. The settings that follow it are builder steps too: a default consumer group, librdkafka properties through config, and the startup and shutdown bounds. A property the service leaves unset keeps the librdkafka default. At startup the runtime connects the broker and receives a ConnectedKafkaBroker. The connect probes the cluster, so an unreachable cluster fails startup instead of the first publish. Every subscription and every publisher of the service opens against that connected form. At shutdown the runtime turns it into a ClosedKafkaBroker, after the producer has flushed what the handlers published. #[subscriber("orders")] reads the topic orders in the broker's default group. Kafka reads a topic only through a consumer group, so a subscription with no group of its own on a broker with no default group fails startup. The descriptors that set a group, several topics or exact partitions per subscription are on the Subscriptions pages.

The service reads the topic orders in the group orders-svc. cargo run --example kafka_quickstart --features testing -- run starts it against a cluster on localhost:9092. Macros Manual examples/kafka_quickstart.rs use ruststream_rdkafka::prelude::*; #[subscriber("orders")] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { b.include(place); }, ) } examples/manual/kafka_quickstart.rs use ruststream_rdkafka::prelude::*; struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders", Place).build()); }, ) }

config and producer_config pass any librdkafka property to every client of the broker or to its producer only. A property set with config reaches every consumer and the producer the broker creates. A property that applies to one side only is ignored by the other, as librdkafka ignores it. producer_config applies on top of config, to the producer alone: acks, compression.type, message.max.bytes, linger.ms. A descriptor's own config adds consumer properties for one subscription. The names and values are librdkafka's, listed in its CONFIGURATION.md. librdkafka checks every property when the broker connects. An unknown name or a value it refuses fails startup with KafkaError::Connect, so a typo never reaches the first publish. The in-process cluster a TestApp test runs on reads the same properties. It refuses what librdkafka refuses, and a record over the producer's message.max.bytes is refused there as on a cluster.

The broker names its clients orders-svc and compresses what it publishes. A shipment over 64 KiB is refused, and the order that produced it is settled as a retry. Macros Manual examples/kafka_broker_config.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { let broker = KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]) .default_group("orders-svc") // Every client: the consumers and the producer. .config("client.id", "orders-svc") .config("socket.keepalive.enable", "true") // The producer only. .producer_config("compression.type", "lz4") .producer_config("message.max.bytes", "65536"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(ship); }) } examples/manual/kafka_broker_config.rs fn app() -> impl App { let broker = KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]) .default_group("orders-svc") // Every client: the consumers and the producer. .config("client.id", "orders-svc") .config("socket.keepalive.enable", "true") // The producer only. .producer_config("compression.type", "lz4") .producer_config("message.max.bytes", "65536"); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders", Ship).reply().build()); }) }

KafkaError is the one error type of the crate: connect, publish, consume, transactions, the registry and the wire format. Each variant names the step that failed. The librdkafka error behind it is its source, so the client library's types stay out of the crate's API. Variant When Connect the client could not be created, a property was refused, or the cluster did not answer the startup probe Subscribe a consumer could not be created or subscribed, or its group did not assign it partitions in time Consume an open consumer failed to receive Publish the cluster refused a record or did not confirm it, or the shutdown flush ran out of time Closed a publisher or a transaction was used after the broker shut down InvalidOptions the settings cannot work together, such as a subscription with no consumer group TransactionBusy, NoTransaction a transaction was begun twice on one publisher, or ended with none open SchemaRegistry, SchemaRegistryTimeout a registry request failed or went unanswered (schema-registry feature) WireFormat a value did not match its Avro or Protobuf wire form (schema-registry feature) A service meets the error in two places. A failed startup carries it as the source of the runtime's error, and the service exits before it reads anything. A publish from a handler returns it inside the core's PublishError, and the handler decides how the delivery settles. The enum is #[non_exhaustive], so a match on it ends with a wildcard arm.

A shipment the cluster refuses is logged with its cause, and the order is settled as a retry. Macros Manual examples/kafka_broker_errors.rs #[subscriber("orders")] async fn ship(order: &Order, Out(shipments): Out<impl Publisher, Shipments>) -> HandlerOutcome { let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id, labels: (1..=order.parcels) .map(|parcel| format!("{}-{parcel:05}", order.id)) .collect(), }; if let Err(err) = shipments.message(&shipment).publish().await { // The error names the topic and the cluster's reason. tracing::warn!(subscription = "orders", order.id, error = %err, "shipment not published"); return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/kafka_broker_errors.rs struct Ship; impl<Entry> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Entry,)>> for Ship where Entry: OutEntry<Shipments, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id, labels: (1..=order.parcels) .map(|parcel| format!("{}-{parcel:05}", order.id)) .collect(), }; if let Err(err) = outs.get(Shipments).message(&shipment).publish().await { // The error names the topic and the cluster's reason. tracing::warn!(subscription = "orders", order.id, error = %err, "shipment not published"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } Ok(()) } }

One glob, ruststream_rdkafka::prelude, brings the core prelude, the descriptors, the policies under concept names and the context keys. use ruststream_rdkafka::prelude::*; is the one import a Kafka service writes. It carries the core's own prelude, so #[subscriber], RustStream, HandlerOutcome and Out come with it. It adds KafkaBroker, the descriptors KafkaTopic, KafkaTopics and KafkaPartitions with their settings (Commit, StartOffset, Assignment, LaneKey), the reply transforms RoundRobin and ToSourceTopic, and the context keys Topic, Partition, Position, Source and SeekHandle. The publish policies come under the names every broker crate uses: Publish is KafkaPublish, TransactionalPublish is KafkaTransactionalPublish, PartitionedPublish is KafkaPartitionedPublish, and EosPublish is KafkaEosPublish. So a mount site reads the same on every broker. Two broker preludes in one file collide on these names; the prefixed types at the crate root tell them apart. A handler body bounds its slots with capability traits, such as Out<impl TransactionalPublisher>, and names no broker type. The one exception is a body that sets a per-record setting: partition(..) needs KafkaPublishSteps in scope and the slot bounded Out<impl Publisher<Options = KafkaOptions>, Marker>, both from this prelude.

The descriptor, its settings and the reply policy all come from the one glob. Macros Manual examples/kafka_broker_prelude.rs use ruststream_rdkafka::prelude::*; #[subscriber( KafkaTopic::new("orders") .group("orders-svc") .commit(Commit::Tracked) .start(StartOffset::Earliest), reply )] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Confirmation { Confirmation { id: order.id } } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]), |b| { b.include(confirm).out_reply(Publish::default()); }, ) } examples/manual/kafka_broker_prelude.rs use ruststream_rdkafka::prelude::*; struct Confirm; impl Handle<Order, Confirmation> for Confirm { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Confirmation, HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(Confirmation { id: order.id })) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]), |b| { let confirm = subscriber("orders", Confirm).map_source(|_| { KafkaTopic::new("orders") .group("orders-svc") .commit(Commit::Tracked) .start(StartOffset::Earliest) }); b.include(confirm.reply().build()) .out_reply(Publish::default()); }, ) }

SASL and TLS are librdkafka properties set through config; the ssl and ssl-vendored features link the OpenSSL they need. security.protocol picks the listener: PLAINTEXT, SSL, SASL_PLAINTEXT or SASL_SSL. sasl.mechanism, sasl.username and sasl.password set the SASL login, and the ssl.* properties the certificates. The bootstrap servers are the addresses of the listener the protocol speaks to. On the default features, librdkafka carries one SASL mechanism, PLAIN. The ssl feature links the system OpenSSL, and ssl-vendored builds OpenSSL from source; either one adds TLS and the SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512 and OAUTHBEARER mechanisms. Without it, a TLS property fails startup with "OpenSSL not available at build time", and a SCRAM or OAUTHBEARER mechanism fails the connect. The zstd feature adds that compression codec; the other codecs are built in. A misspelled security.protocol fails startup, in a TestApp test as on a cluster. The generated AsyncAPI document reports the bootstrap addresses and never the credentials.

The dependency line: ruststream-rdkafka = { version = "0.7", features = ["ssl"] } The service authenticates with SCRAM over TLS and verifies the cluster against its own certificate authority. The password comes from the environment. Macros Manual examples/kafka_broker_security.rs /// The cluster's `SASL_SSL` listener, with the service's own credentials. fn broker(password: &str, ca: &str) -> KafkaBroker { KafkaBroker::new(["kafka-1.internal:9093", "kafka-2.internal:9093"]) .default_group("orders-svc") .config("security.protocol", "SASL_SSL") .config("sasl.mechanism", "SCRAM-SHA-512") .config("sasl.username", "orders-svc") .config("sasl.password", password) .config("ssl.ca.location", ca) } /// The service, with the password and the certificate authority the deployment hands it. fn service(password: &str, ca: &str) -> impl App + use<> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker(password, ca), |b| { b.include(place); }) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { service( &env::var("KAFKA_PASSWORD").unwrap_or_default(), "/etc/kafka/ca.pem", ) } examples/manual/kafka_broker_security.rs /// The cluster's `SASL_SSL` listener, with the service's own credentials. fn broker(password: &str, ca: &str) -> KafkaBroker { KafkaBroker::new(["kafka-1.internal:9093", "kafka-2.internal:9093"]) .default_group("orders-svc") .config("security.protocol", "SASL_SSL") .config("sasl.mechanism", "SCRAM-SHA-512") .config("sasl.username", "orders-svc") .config("sasl.password", password) .config("ssl.ca.location", ca) } /// The service, with the password and the certificate authority the deployment hands it. fn service(password: &str, ca: &str) -> impl App + use<> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker(password, ca), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders", Place).build()); }) } fn app() -> impl App { service( &env::var("KAFKA_PASSWORD").unwrap_or_default(), "/etc/kafka/ca.pem", ) }

Shutdown flushes in-flight publishes within flush_timeout, and a publisher used afterwards reports KafkaError::Closed. librdkafka sends records in the background, so a publish the cluster has not yet confirmed may still sit in the producer's queue. At shutdown the runtime closes the connection first and then flushes that queue. The flush waits up to flush_timeout, 30 seconds by default. Records still queued after it fail the shutdown with KafkaError::Publish. A service that never published has no producer and nothing to flush. A publisher taken before the shutdown keeps pointing at the closed connection. A publish through it, or a commit or an abort of its transaction, returns KafkaError::Closed with the topic or the transactional id, and never succeeds against the dead connection. A tool that drives the broker by hand receives a ClosedKafkaBroker from the shutdown; its unflushed_records is the number of records librdkafka still held.

The flush gets ten seconds, and the shipments the handler replied with reach the cluster before the service exits. Macros Manual examples/kafka_broker_shutdown.rs /// The cluster at `servers`; shutdown waits up to ten seconds for in-flight records. fn broker(servers: &str) -> KafkaBroker { KafkaBroker::new([servers]) .default_group("orders-svc") .flush_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { service(broker("localhost:9092")) } examples/manual/kafka_broker_shutdown.rs /// The cluster at `servers`; shutdown waits up to ten seconds for in-flight records. fn broker(servers: &str) -> KafkaBroker { KafkaBroker::new([servers]) .default_group("orders-svc") .flush_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)) } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { service(broker("localhost:9092")) }

Startup probes the cluster within connect_timeout and waits up to assignment_timeout for each group to assign its partitions. The connect fetches the cluster's metadata. A cluster that does not answer within connect_timeout, 30 seconds by default, fails startup with KafkaError::Connect. The connect also checks the producer's properties, and opens no producer: the first publish opens it, so a service that only consumes runs none. A subscription through a consumer group is open once the group has assigned this member its partitions and the offset each one starts from is known. From that moment everything published to the topic reaches it. Startup waits for each group up to assignment_timeout, 60 seconds by default, and then fails with KafkaError::Subscribe, naming the subscription and its group. A new group waits the coordinator's group.initial.rebalance.delay.ms, three seconds by default. A group that still holds a member which left without a word waits until that member's session.timeout.ms expires, 45 seconds by default. A subscription that names its partitions with KafkaPartitions joins no group and does not wait. A subscription to a topic the cluster does not have yet opens without partitions. When the topic appears, the group reads it from where auto.offset.reset puts it, the end of the log by default, so the record that created the topic is not read.

The probe gives up after five seconds, and each group gets twenty seconds to assign its partitions. Macros Manual examples/kafka_broker_startup.rs /// The cluster at `servers`, with both startup waits bounded. fn broker(servers: &str) -> KafkaBroker { KafkaBroker::new([servers]) .default_group("orders-svc") // The reachability probe: a metadata fetch. .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)) // Each consumer group assigning this member its partitions. .assignment_timeout(Duration::from_secs(20)) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { service(broker("localhost:9092")) } examples/manual/kafka_broker_startup.rs /// The cluster at `servers`, with both startup waits bounded. fn broker(servers: &str) -> KafkaBroker { KafkaBroker::new([servers]) .default_group("orders-svc") // The reachability probe: a metadata fetch. .connect_timeout(Duration::from_secs(5)) // Each consumer group assigning this member its partitions. .assignment_timeout(Duration::from_secs(20)) } fn app() -> impl App { service(broker("localhost:9092")) }

KafkaContext gives a handler the record's topic, partition, offset, timestamp and key, each read as a parameter through Ctx<K>. The subscription builds it once per delivery, beside the payload and the headers. A handler binds one field with Ctx<K>, where K is a key of context::keys: Key Value What it is Topic Str the topic the record was read from, which differs per record on a topic list or pattern Partition i32 the partition the record was read from Offset i64 the record's offset in its partition TimestampMillis Option<i64> the record's timestamp in milliseconds since the epoch, when it has one Key Option<Bytes> the record key, when the record has one Topic and Partition are in the prelude; the other keys are imported from context::keys. A body that reads several fields takes ctx: &mut Context<'_, KafkaContext> instead and calls ctx.context(key) per field, as the manual form does. Reading the context also hands it to the retry position, where ToSourceTopic reads the topic. The same context carries the Position and SeekHandle keys, which move the subscription through the log.

Macros Manual examples/kafka_context_fields.rs /// Each `Ctx<K>` binds one field of the record; the order's customer is its record key. #[subscriber(KafkaTopic::new("orders").group("audit"), reply)] async fn audit( order: &Order, Ctx(topic): Ctx<Topic>, Ctx(partition): Ctx<Partition>, Ctx(offset): Ctx<Offset>, Ctx(timestamp_millis): Ctx<TimestampMillis>, Ctx(key): Ctx<Key>, ) -> AuditRecord { let customer = key.map(|key: Bytes| String::from_utf8_lossy(&key).into_owned()); tracing::info!(order.id, %topic, partition, offset, "order audited"); AuditRecord { order_id: order.id, topic: topic.to_string(), partition, offset, timestamp_millis, customer, } } examples/manual/kafka_context_fields.rs /// The body reads each field of the record off its context by its key; the order's customer is /// its record key. struct Audit; impl Handle<Order, AuditRecord, (), KafkaContext> for Audit { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, KafkaContext>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<AuditRecord, HandlerOutcome>> { let topic = ctx.context(Topic).to_string(); let partition = ctx.context(Partition); let offset = ctx.context(Offset); let customer = ctx .context(Key) .map(|key| String::from_utf8_lossy(key).into_owned()); tracing::info!(order.id, %topic, partition, offset, "order audited"); ready(Ok(AuditRecord { order_id: order.id, topic, partition, offset, timestamp_millis: ctx.context(TimestampMillis), customer, })) } } fn audited() -> KafkaTopic { KafkaTopic::new("orders").group("audit") }

A batch handler's context, KafkaBatchContext, carries the subscription's seek handle; each record's own coordinates travel with the elements. A batch spans many records, so it has no single topic, partition or offset. The subscription builds the context once per batch, and it holds what every record of the batch shares: the SeekHandle key, the same key a KafkaContext carries. A batch body takes ctx: &mut Context<'_, KafkaBatchContext> and reads the handle with ctx.context(SeekHandle). A seek from a batch body takes effect once the whole batch has settled, so the next batch opens at the new position. A per-record key such as Partition or Offset is a compile error in a batch body, because the batch context does not carry it. A batch registration has no per-record topic for ToSourceTopic either, so it names a fixed retry topic.

Macros Manual examples/kafka_context_batch.rs /// The batch settles first; the seek then opens the next batch at the offset a job named, so /// the run from there is processed again. #[subscriber(KafkaTopic::new("jobs").group("jobs-svc").commit(Commit::Tracked))] async fn drain( jobs: &[Job], ctx: &mut Context<'_, KafkaBatchContext>, State(redos): State<Arc<Redos>>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(jobs = jobs.len(), "draining jobs"); let target = jobs .iter() .filter(|job| redos.first_time(job)) .find_map(|job| job.redo_from); if let Some((partition, offset)) = target && ctx .context(SeekHandle) .seek(KafkaPosition::offset(partition, offset)) .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/kafka_context_batch.rs /// The batch settles first; the seek then opens the next batch at the offset a job named, so /// the run from there is processed again. struct Drain; impl Handle<[Job], (), (), KafkaBatchContext, AppState> for Drain { async fn handle( &self, jobs: &[Job], _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, KafkaBatchContext, AppState>, ) -> Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(jobs = jobs.len(), "draining jobs"); let redos = &ctx.state().redos; let target = jobs .iter() .filter(|job| redos.first_time(job)) .find_map(|job| job.redo_from); if let Some((partition, offset)) = target && ctx .context(SeekHandle) .seek(KafkaPosition::offset(partition, offset)) .await .is_err() { return Err(jobs.iter().map(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()).collect()); } Ok(()) } } fn jobs() -> KafkaTopic { KafkaTopic::new("jobs") .group("jobs-svc") .commit(Commit::Tracked) }

KafkaPosition names a place in the log: either end, an offset, an offset of one topic, or a timestamp. Kafka keeps its log, so a subscription can be moved through it, at startup with start_at or from a handler with a seek. KafkaPosition::earliest() is the oldest record each partition retains, and KafkaPosition::latest() is the end of each partition's log. KafkaPosition::timestamp(millis) is, on each partition, the first record stamped at or after that time in epoch milliseconds; a partition with no such record resumes at its end. These three apply to every partition the subscription reads. KafkaPosition::offset(partition, offset) is one partition at an absolute offset, on every topic the subscription reads. KafkaPosition::topic_offset(topic, partition, offset) names the topic too, which a subscription over several topics needs. A delivery's own coordinates are a position as well: Ctx<Position> binds them, and a seek there replays that record. A position on a partition or a topic the subscription does not read is refused with an error.

A new reporting group starts from the first reading stamped at or after the time its configuration names. Macros Manual examples/kafka_positions_timestamp.rs /// Totals meter readings. #[subscriber("metering.readings")] async fn total(reading: &Reading) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(reading.id, "totalled"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } /// The service, reading from the first record stamped at or after `since` (epoch milliseconds). fn app(servers: &str, group: &str, since: i64) -> impl App<State = ()> { let broker = KafkaBroker::new([servers]).default_group(group); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("metering", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(total.start_at(KafkaPosition::timestamp(since))); }) } examples/manual/kafka_positions_timestamp.rs /// Totals meter readings. struct Total; impl Handle<Reading> for Total { fn handle( &self, reading: &Reading, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(reading.id, "totalled"); ready(Ok(())) } } /// The service, reading from the first record stamped at or after `since` (epoch milliseconds). fn app(servers: &str, group: &str, since: i64) -> impl App<State = ()> { let broker = KafkaBroker::new([servers]).default_group(group); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("metering", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include( subscriber("metering.readings", Total) .start_at(KafkaPosition::timestamp(since)) .build(), ); }) }

A handler moves its running subscription through the SeekHandle key; the seek is local and a rebalance discards it. Ctx<SeekHandle> binds a KafkaSeeker for the subscription the delivery came from. Its seek(position) takes a KafkaPosition, and the next delivery comes from there. Ctx<Partition> and Ctx<Position> give the delivery's own coordinates to aim with. A seek moves this consumer and no other member of the group. It commits nothing, and the next rebalance discards it: whoever gets the partitions resumes from the group's committed offsets. Under Commit::Tracked a seek clears the tracked position of every partition it moves, so a later commit never passes records the seek replayed and nobody handled. A seek after the service shut down returns an error. A batch handler reaches the same key through its KafkaBatchContext, and the move applies once the batch has settled. A position that has to survive a restart belongs in start_at instead.

A job that carries resume_at moves its partition past a run of jobs known to fail. Macros Manual examples/kafka_seek.rs /// Skips a run of jobs known to fail: the partition jumps to `resume_at`. #[subscriber(KafkaTopic::new("jobs").group("jobs-svc").commit(Commit::Tracked))] async fn work( job: &Job, Ctx(partition): Ctx<Partition>, Ctx(seeker): Ctx<SeekHandle>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(job.id, "worked"); let Some(resume_at) = job.resume_at else { return HandlerOutcome::ack(); }; match seeker .seek(KafkaPosition::offset(partition, resume_at)) .await { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(_) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), } } examples/manual/kafka_seek.rs /// Skips a run of jobs known to fail: the partition jumps to `resume_at`. struct Work; impl Handle<Job, (), (), KafkaContext> for Work { async fn handle( &self, job: &Job, _outs: &(), ctx: &mut Context<'_, KafkaContext>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { tracing::info!(job.id, "worked"); let Some(resume_at) = job.resume_at else { return Ok(()); }; let position = KafkaPosition::offset(ctx.context(Partition), resume_at); ctx.context(SeekHandle) .seek(position) .await .map_err(|_| HandlerOutcome::retry()) } } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { let broker = KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("jobs", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let jobs = KafkaTopic::new("jobs") .group("jobs-svc") .commit(Commit::Tracked); b.include(subscriber("jobs", Work).build().map_source(|_| jobs)); }) }

start_at opens a subscription at a position on every startup, whatever the group committed. It is a clause of the attribute, start_at(KafkaPosition::earliest()), or .start_at(position) among the mount-site settings. The position lands on the partitions the subscription opened with, ahead of their first record. A subscription that opened with no partitions takes the position on the first assignment its group hands over. Under Assignment::CooperativeSticky that first assignment may be part of the group's share, and partitions that arrive in a later increment start from the committed offset. A position that names none of the partitions the subscription opened with stops the service at startup. It suits a read model rebuilt from the retained log on each boot. A group's start offset is different: it applies only where the group has committed nothing.

The audit projection is rebuilt from the oldest retained entry on every startup, although its group committed everything it read before. Macros Manual examples/kafka_seek.rs /// Rebuilds the audit projection from the oldest retained entry on every startup. #[subscriber( KafkaTopic::new("ledger.audit").commit(Commit::Tracked), start_at(KafkaPosition::earliest()) )] async fn replay(entry: &AuditEntry) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(entry.id, "projected"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/kafka_seek.rs /// Projects every audit entry it reads. struct Replay; impl Handle<AuditEntry> for Replay { fn handle( &self, entry: &AuditEntry, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(entry.id, "projected"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app(servers: &str, group: &str) -> impl App<State = ()> { let broker = KafkaBroker::new([servers]).default_group(group); RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("audit", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let audit = KafkaTopic::new("ledger.audit").commit(Commit::Tracked); // The projection is rebuilt from the oldest retained entry on every startup. b.include( subscriber("ledger.audit", Replay) .build() .map_source(|_| audit) .start_at(KafkaPosition::earliest()), ); }) }

A prost message rides the byte lanes as itself, and decode_confluent steps over the Confluent envelope with no registry. The protobuf feature adds it, with the protobuf module. A generated message is not a serde type, so it carries its own bytes: an incoming type derives Deserialized and names #[wire(decode = decode_confluent)], an outgoing one derives Serialized and names #[wire(encode = prost::Message::encode)]. The handler then takes and returns generated messages, and its signature says nothing about the wire. A registry-backed producer writes the Confluent envelope in front of the message: a zero byte, the four-byte schema id, and the index path of the message within its schema. decode_confluent parses all three and reads the rest into the reader's own type. No lookup is needed, because Protobuf fields are addressed by tag: an unknown field is kept as unknown, and a missing one takes its default. A payload with no envelope is read as a bare message, so a topic where only some producers frame still decodes. What the reader does not check is which schema version a delivery claims. Writing the envelope needs the schema id of the destination's subject, which a value cannot look up. The publish side adds it where the destination is known: framed at a mount site, or ProtobufFrame for the whole app. A publish without either sends the bare message. A subject is registered from .proto text through SchemaRegistry::register with SchemaType::Protobuf. The registry paths compile that text with the well-known types available, so a schema imports from them and from nothing else.

The generated types, with their lanes. examples/kafka_protobuf_plain.rs // What `prost-build` emits, plus the lane derives: the order decodes past the envelope, and the // confirmation encodes itself through `prost`. #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, prost::Message, Deserialized)] #[wire(decode = decode_confluent)] struct Order { #[prost(int64, tag = "1")] id: i64, #[prost(string, tag = "2")] item: String, } #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, prost::Message, Serialized, Outgoing)] #[wire(encode = prost::Message::encode)] #[outgoing(name = "confirmations")] struct Confirmation { #[prost(int64, tag = "1")] id: i64, #[prost(bool, tag = "2")] accepted: bool, } The handler reads a framed or a bare order and returns the confirmation, which leaves as a bare message. Macros Manual examples/kafka_protobuf_plain.rs /// Confirms an order that names an item. #[subscriber("orders", reply)] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Confirmation { tracing::info!(order = order.id, item = %order.item, "confirming"); Confirmation { id: order.id, accepted: !order.item.is_empty(), } } examples/manual/kafka_protobuf_plain.rs /// Confirms an order that names an item. struct Confirm; // Both positions are generated messages that carry their own bytes, so neither names a codec. impl Handle<Order, Confirmation> for Confirm { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Confirmation, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order = order.id, item = %order.item, "confirming"); ready(Ok(Confirmation { id: order.id, accepted: !order.item.is_empty(), })) } } Macros Manual examples/kafka_protobuf_plain.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { b.include(confirm); }, ) } examples/manual/kafka_protobuf_plain.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders", Confirm).reply().build()); }, ) }

KafkaPublish::framed puts the Confluent envelope on every message its policy publishes, with the destination subject's schema id. It returns a KafkaFramedPublish, a policy like any other, so it goes where a policy goes: .out_reply(..) or an Out slot. Its live form is a KafkaFramedPublisher. The subject comes from the destination topic, {topic}-value by default; subject_strategy and subject choose another. The index path names the schema's first message, which Confluent writes as one zero byte. message pins another message of the schema by its full name, for a topic whose type is not declared first. KafkaFramedPublish::over wraps a configured KafkaPublish instead of the default one. The subject is resolved on the first publish to each destination and cached. That is the first moment the destination is known: it comes from the reply clause or the slot publish, not from the policy. So a subject the registry does not hold, or one holding another format, fails that publish with the subject and the format, and the handler's failure policy settles the delivery. A payload that already carries an envelope is left as it is, so the policy and ProtobufFrame together frame a message once.

The receipt declares no destination, so the mount site's reply("order-receipts") names it, and the policy frames it with the id of order-receipts-value. Macros Manual examples/kafka_protobuf_framed.rs // The receipt names no destination, so the mount site's `reply(..)` does. #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, prost::Message, Serialized, Outgoing)] #[wire(encode = prost::Message::encode)] struct Receipt { #[prost(int64, tag = "1")] order_id: i64, #[prost(bool, tag = "2")] accepted: bool, } #[subscriber("orders", reply("order-receipts"))] async fn receipt(order: &Order) -> Receipt { Receipt { order_id: order.id, accepted: !order.item.is_empty(), } } examples/manual/kafka_protobuf_framed.rs // The receipt names no destination, so the mount site's `reply(..)` does. #[derive(Clone, PartialEq, prost::Message, Serialized, Outgoing)] #[wire(encode = prost::Message::encode)] struct Receipt { #[prost(int64, tag = "1")] order_id: i64, #[prost(bool, tag = "2")] accepted: bool, } struct Confirm; impl Handle<Order, Receipt> for Confirm { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Receipt, HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(Receipt { order_id: order.id, accepted: !order.item.is_empty(), })) } } Macros Manual examples/kafka_protobuf_framed.rs fn app(registry: &SchemaRegistry) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { // The subject is the destination topic's, `order-receipts-value`, resolved on the // first reply and cached. b.include(receipt).out_reply(Publish::framed(registry)); }, ) } examples/manual/kafka_protobuf_framed.rs fn app(registry: &SchemaRegistry) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { let orders = subscriber("orders", Confirm).reply().to("order-receipts"); // The subject is the destination topic's, `order-receipts-value`, resolved on the // first reply and cached. b.include(orders.build()) .out_reply(Publish::framed(registry)); }, ) }

ProtobufFrame, added with publish_layer, frames every Protobuf publish of the app that leaves through a slot. ProtobufFrame::new takes the registry, and the app adds the layer once, so no mount site names the framing. A publish is framed when its destination's subject holds a Protobuf schema. Every other publish passes as it is: a topic with no subject, and a subject holding Avro or JSON. So one app carries Protobuf, Avro and JSON topics with the layer installed. A payload that already carries an envelope also passes, so a message is never framed twice. subject_strategy, subject and message choose the subject and the message as they do on framed. The layer sees what leaves through an Out slot and through a publisher the runtime pairs. A reply returned from a reply(..) handler goes straight to its paired publisher, so it is framed by naming framed at its mount site. The layer is an alternative to the transcode's SchemaFrame: this one expects the payload to be the Protobuf datum already, that one expects JSON.

Every order writes an audit record through a slot, and the layer frames it with the id of order-audit-value. Macros Manual examples/kafka_protobuf_frame.rs #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Audit)] struct Journal; /// Records every order in the audit journal; the app's layer frames the record. #[subscriber("orders")] async fn audit(order: &Order, Out(journal): Out<impl Publisher, Journal>) -> HandlerOutcome { let record = Audit { order_id: order.id }; if journal.message(&record).publish().await.is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/kafka_protobuf_frame.rs struct Journal; impl OutSlot for Journal { const NAME: &'static str = "Journal"; type Destination = Reads; } impl PublishedThrough<Journal> for Audit {} /// Records every order in the audit journal; the app's layer frames the record. struct AuditOrder; impl<J> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(J,)>> for AuditOrder where J: OutEntry<Journal, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(J,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let record = Audit { order_id: order.id }; if outs.get(Journal).message(&record).publish().await.is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } Ok(()) } } Macros Manual examples/kafka_protobuf_frame.rs fn app(registry: &SchemaRegistry) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) // Frames every publish whose destination subject holds a Protobuf schema. .publish_layer(ProtobufFrame::new(registry.clone())) .with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { b.include(audit).out(Journal, Publish::default()).build(); }, ) } examples/manual/kafka_protobuf_frame.rs fn app(registry: &SchemaRegistry) -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) // Frames every publish whose destination subject holds a Protobuf schema. .publish_layer(ProtobufFrame::new(registry.clone())) .with_broker( KafkaBroker::new(["localhost:9092"]).default_group("orders-svc"), |b| { b.include(subscriber("orders", AuditOrder).build()) .out(Journal, Publish::default()) .build(); }, ) }

On a broker with schema_registry, framed Protobuf arrives as JSON and leaves framed, with no generated code in the service. Every subscription of that broker reads a delivery's schema id, fetches the schema and compiles its .proto source into a descriptor. It decodes the datum into a dynamic message and hands the handler JSON, so the handler is a plain serde one on the default codec. On the way out, the SchemaFrame publish layer turns the JSON into the subject's Protobuf message and frames it. Field names in the serde types match the .proto messages. The message written is the schema's first; SchemaFrame::message pins another. This path is for a service that does not carry generated types. It costs a JSON hop and a dynamic message per delivery, and nothing decodes while the registry is unreachable. A service with generated types reads them on the byte lanes with decode_confluent instead. The two do not mix on one broker: a broker with schema_registry transcodes every subscription, so a generated type there would be handed JSON.
